events.title: OCaml language released
events.summary: On May 9, 1996, Xavier Leroy released OCaml 1.00 — a fast, type-safe language combining functional programming with objects and modules.
events.about: OCaml catches many bugs at compile time through strong types and pattern matching, while staying practical for systems work. Jane Street uses it for trading systems; it powers parts of the Coq proof assistant ecosystem and lightweight operating systems. It influenced F#, Rust's safety ideas, and verified software research.

narrative.whyChosen: OCaml 1.00 was the first public release to combine objects with ML-style type safety and a production-speed native compiler.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the go-to industrial ML-family language — influencing F#, Rust, and formally verified software.
narrative.problemSolved: The previous Caml dialect needed objects without giving up the static safety and module system researchers relied on.
